extraction.pages_processed: 10, 12, 25-27, 63, 66-68, 76 read; keyword screen of the whole text
extraction.notes: RUN-2026-02 comparator step (P4 step 4, LIM-0048): RI-FMW-015, RI-TEC-038 and RI-TEC-036 (update of case CMP-0009). Read the main findings for the economic criteria, Chapter 5 and Chapter 2 (pages 10, 12), public administration reform service delivery (page 27), the economic criteria passages on e-services (pages 63, 66), the detailed Chapter 5 section (pages 67-68) and the detailed Chapter 2 section (page 76); screened the whole text for electronic procurement, EHIC, health insurance, health information, e-government, portal, e-services, electronic services, digital services and transactional (also with spaces removed). Text-file page numbers are printed page numbers plus one. Not extracted: the Chapter 2 preparation level and the provisional closure in June 2026 (page 12: chapter-level); the Chapter 5 rating 'Some progress' (page 10); the share of centralised procurement, 3% in 2023 to 27% in 2025 (page 67: no link to the electronic system stated); the EESSI and EURES material (page 76); the Government Service Bus, register interconnection and eID sentences (pages 27, 63: other issues); e-Participation and e-Petitions portals (page 26) and the Point of Single Contact portal (page 12, 77: sector system); the citizens' satisfaction sentence (page 27: public services in general, no digital element). The 2026 key recommendation on digital public services no longer asks for an interactive e-government platform (compare MNE-EU-2025-001-0007).
